messages:
carla: OK team — kicking off a quick thread on long-term topology for routing + multi-tenant isolation. Two recent customer asks (BankCo, AdsCorp) push us toward stronger regional residency + tenant isolation. Need quick alignment on launch criteria and what we scope into the pilot.

raj: +1. What are the hard perf/ops numbers we want to hold for pilot? p95 latency, autoscale windows, and SLO for fallback behavior.

mei: High level: phase by risk. pilot(1-2 customers) -> controlled ramp (selected customers) -> GA. Key constraints: regional affinity, model-variant fallbacks, tenant thinning to avoid noisy neighbors.

jonas: For pilot we should commit to: p95 <= 350ms for small prompts, cold-start <= 1200ms, and circuit-breaker behavior documented. Ops: runbook for tenant evacuation.

carla: Good. Proposal for launch-criteria doc snippet:
```
- Pilot: 2 customers onboarded + runbook verified
- SLOs: p95 latency target + error rate < 0.5%
- Safety: data residency validated + KMS integration tested
- Rollout: canary traffic at 5% for 48h -> 25% for 72h -> full
```
Anyone object?

tom: Sales note: BankCo needs explicit SLA language on residency and isolation before committing to reserved capacity. Also wants pricing visibility for dedicated slices. We should get legal + sales to approve wording before GA. @lina FYI for compliance.

lina: A couple security red flags: cross-tenant cache leakage risk, KMS audit trail gaps for private deployments. Need acceptance tests for both. Also require penetration test plan for pilot.

alex_cs: From CS: BankCo will take pilot if we can promise a single-region tenant lane and a migration plan to multi-region later. AdsCorp is ok with shared lanes if throughput is guaranteed. We can use both as complementary pilots.

mei: Operationally we need policy precedence: 1) tenant region override, 2) model variant selection, 3) cost-based fallback. That will determine routing decisions. Example policy snippet: 
```yaml
routing_policy:
  prefer_region: customer_region
  fallback: compatible_model_variant
  max_latency_budget_ms: 600
```
This keeps behavior deterministic.

jonas: Implementation note: runtime can enforce `max_latency_budget_ms` by switching to smaller kv-cache-preserving models for long tails. We should quantify quality delta for fallback models as part of launch.

raj: Dependency list: infra quota for dedicated lanes, autoscaler changes for tenant-aware batching, telemetry hooks for per-tenant p95. Who owns telemetry? @jonas or infra team?

jonas: I can prototype tenant-level telemetry but we'll need a small infra change to the ingestion pipeline (obfuscation + tenant tags).

carla: Decisions we need this week: (1) Pilot customers and phasing (BankCo + AdsCorp OK?), (2) Concrete SLOs to commit, (3) Security acceptance test list, (4) Contract language draft for sales/legal.

tom: Yes on pilots. I'll get draft SLA language ready by EOD Thu.

lina: I'll put together the security acceptance checklist and pen-test scoping doc by Friday.

alex_cs: I'll coordinate onboarding runbooks with the two customers and collect their acceptance criteria.

raj: Engineering can commit to prototype telemetry + basic autoscale changes for pilot by the end of next sprint. Can we treat GA gating as: all pilot blockers cleared + 2 week stability window at 25% traffic?

mei: That gating sounds reasonable. Also recommend a rollback plan: auto-evacuate affected tenants to shared fallback region and route to hosted model variants.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new branch rtx/isolation-pilot created, CI passed, 3/5 integration checks pending. :gear:

carla: Great — I'll consolidate these action items into a short PRD and tag owners. Quick ask: add one line to that PRD clarifying cost delta for dedicated slices vs shared lanes so Sales can discuss with customers.

tom: Will add cost delta table. :thumbsup:

jonas: I'll start a prototype lab and post short perf numbers in this thread when available.

carla: Thanks all — we can reconvene if any blocker surfaces. Keeping thread for the action items and status updates.
